title: FiftyK activation slice — payg + starter heuristics
content:
Quick brain-dump: a lightweight 'first 50k tokens' activation subsidy sketch for PLG funnel experiments.

Goal: subsidize the first 50k tokens for new accounts to lower the time-to-value and nudge early product exploration. Keep subsidy cheap but visible in console.

Assumptions (very rough):
- Avg tokens per call: 200 tokens
- Active calls/day (first 30d window): 5
- Active days in 30d: 10 (so ~50 calls -> 10k tokens)
- Activation credit target: 50,000 tokens (covers bursts + a few evals)
- Placeholder marginal hosted cost: $0.005 / 1k tokens (conservative for small batch/low-efficiency cases)

Back-of-envelope math:
- Cost to Redwood per user for 50k tokens = (50k / 1k) * $0.005 = 50 * 0.005 = $0.25
- If 10k users redeem full credit -> infra cost = $2,500 (not big if acquisition is targeted)

GPU-hour amortization (sketch to sanity-check):
- Blended infra cost (example): $2.5 / hour (per equivalent serving blade)
- Throughput guess: 24M tokens / hour (depends hugely on model / batch / kv cache) -> cost per 1k tokens = 2.5 / 24000 = $0.000104 (best-case)
- Realistic conservative per-1k picked above ($0.005) to account for small deployments, overhead, smaller models, tails.

Conversion sensitivity thought-experiment:
- If activation credit yields +3% absolute conversion uplift (from freemium->paid) and average revenue per converting user in 90d = $120, subsidy is very cheap.
- If uplift is tiny (<0.5%) then cost of credits must be weighed against CAC and fraud.

Tiering ideas with activation built-in:
- Starter (free): 50k activation tokens, 30d expiry, low rate limits. Shows in console as "activation credits remaining" (strong UX signal).
- Microcommit: $10-$25/mo -> includes 200k tokens + activation rolled in; easy anchor from free->paid.
- PAYG: after activation, charged per 1k tokens with soft volume discounts (100k+, 500k+).

Product levers to increase effective ROI:
- Staircase release: release credits in 10k blocks to create visible progress and incremental nudges.
- Timebox: 30d expiration increases urgency to convert.
- Onboarding templates: pre-built prompts that encourage early heavy usage (embedding playgrounds, retrieval demos).
- Conditional unlocks: require verifying email + phone or uploading a milestone app to get extra 50k (fraud mitigation).

Risks and unknowns:
- Fraud/gaming: bots creating accounts just to burn free credits. Need heuristics (card verification, device/IP signals, rate thresholds).
- SKU variance: different models have wildly different per-token cost; activation must be model-agnostic or gated by model family.
- Behavioral: subsidized usage might not correlate with sticky product behavior — could just inflate one-off experiments.

Needed data & next steps:
- Ask growth-metrics for 7/14/30d token distribution for new accounts (median + 90th pct).
- Ask runtime/serving team for per-1k token cost by model class (small/med/large) at current fleet mix.
- Simulate economics: input CPA scenarios (e.g., $5/$20/$50), conversion lift assumptions (0.5%/3%/10%), LTV windows (90d, 365d).
- Prototype console UX: show credits, progress bar, expiry date; A/B test visibility vs control.

Quick simulation notes (scratch numbers):
- Subsidy cost per redeemed user = $0.25
- If 1,000 new signups -> expected redemption rate 30% -> cost = 300 * 0.25 = $75 -> trivial relative to acquisition.
- If redemption -> 3% conversion to paid -> 30 conversions -> revenue @ $120 = $3,600 -> net positive after subsidy even with modest CAC.

Implementation considerations:
- Track credit issuance + redemption in billing ledger (tie to account id + reason = "activation-credit-50k").
- Prevent automated refresh: throttle credits per device/email/IP and require slight frictions for mass issuance.
- Make credits visible in API + SDK (headers or billing endpoint) so developers can instrument.

To do (shorthand):
- [ ] pull new-account token hist (growth-metrics)
- [ ] get per-1k by model class (serving-runtime)
- [ ] draft experiment spec (growth + product) for cohort test
- [ ] design console UI mock (DX) + messaging copy for email nudges

Open questions I want answered before we prototype:
- Break-even CPA thresholds for 3/5/10% conversion lifts
- Operational cost of fraud mitigation vs. subsidy size
- Whether to make activation model-restricted (e.g., only on small/medium models)

Random scribbles/ideas:
- Visual: progress bar + "you've used X/50k activation tokens" + CTA to upgrade before expiry
- Behavioral nudge: "10k tokens unlocked when you connect your first repo" (ties to product usage)
- Billing: consider converting leftover activation into a discount when they upgrade (partial carry-over?) — pros/cons on accounting complexity.

End notes: this is intentionally loose. Keep subsidy slender (~$0.25/user) and instrument heavily. If we can show a reliable lift to conversion, scale up.
